How many medspas owners buy courses

If you want to sell med spa owners, you have to stop thinking about the **surface problem** and sell to the **emotional problem** they're living with every day.

These are the pain points they actually feel:

### Financial fear
- "I made $100k this month and somehow I still don't have money."
- Payroll is due.
- Product invoices are due.
- Ads are expensive.
- They don't know if next month will be better.

### They feel trapped
- They own a business that owns them.
- They can't take a vacation.
- Every emergency lands on their desk.
- If they stop working, revenue slows down.

### They don't trust their team
- Nobody sells like they do.
- Front desk doesn't follow up.
- Providers don't educate patients.
- Everyone says they're "too busy."

### Marketing frustration
- They've spent tens of thousands on agencies.
- Leads come in...
- Patients ghost.
- Cheap Botox shoppers waste everyone's time.
- They have no idea what's actually working.

### Patient retention
- They spend hundreds of dollars to acquire a patient...
- The patient buys one treatment...
- Then disappears forever.
- They know they're leaving thousands on the table but don't know how to fix it. Repeat business is one of the biggest drivers of profitability in med spas. citeturn0search10turn0search6

### Staffing
This is consistently one of the biggest concerns owners report.
- Can't find injectors.
- Can't keep injectors.
- Front desk turnover.
- Constant training.
- Team drama.
- Employees leave and take clients with them. citeturn0search1turn0search0

### Decision fatigue
Every day they're deciding:
- Which laser to buy.
- Whether to hire.
- Whether to fire.
- Whether to increase ad spend.
- Whether to lower prices.
- Which vendor is telling the truth.

They're mentally exhausted.

### Comparison
They open Instagram and see competitors "crushing it."

Meanwhile they're wondering:
- "Why am I working harder than everyone else?"
- "Am I doing something wrong?"
- "Why isn't my practice growing?"

### Fear of failure
Many invested their savings.
Some mortgaged their homes.
Some left stable careers.

The thought they rarely say out loud is:
> "What if I fail after everyone believed in me?"

### What they actually want
They don't really want:
- More leads.
- Better ads.
- A CRM.
- AI.

They want:
- Predictable revenue.
- A team they can trust.
- Patients who keep coming back.
- A business that doesn't depend on them every hour.
- The freedom to enjoy the life they built the practice to create.

That last point is the emotional outcome almost every growth-minded owner is chasing. Your messaging becomes much stronger when you sell **freedom, predictability, and confidence** rather than marketing tactics or more appointments.

parts:
The honest answer is: **no one knows exactly.** There isn't an industry report that tracks what percentage of med spa owners buy business courses.

Based on the industry, though, here's a reasonable estimate:

- **80-90%** of med spa owners will **never buy** a business growth course. They rely on YouTube, Facebook groups, conferences, vendor reps, or trial and error.
- **10-20%** will purchase at least one educational product, coaching program, mastermind, or online course during the life of their practice.
- Of those who do buy education, only a small subset (perhaps **2-5% of all owners**) invest repeatedly in premium coaching or implementation programs. These tend to be owners doing $750K+ annually who view education as an investment rather than an expense.

The important distinction is **who** buys.

Most successful course buyers are:
- Growth-minded owners already generating revenue.
- Frustrated because they're stuck between roughly $500K and $2M in annual revenue.
- Looking for systems, leadership, marketing, or operations, not just injector training.

By contrast, **clinical training** (Botox, lasers, injectables, certifications) is a much larger market than **business growth courses**. Market research shows online and hybrid medical aesthetics training continues to grow rapidly, but practice management and marketing education remains a relatively small portion of overall training demand. citeturn0search7turn0search1

For your business, this is actually good news.

You're **not** selling to every med spa owner. The American Med Spa Association estimates that about **90% of med spas are independently owned**, meaning the decision maker is usually the owner sitting in front of you. citeturn0search0

That means your ideal customer is likely the owner who:
- Already spends money to grow (ads, coaching, consultants).
- Knows they're leaking revenue.
- Wants implementation, accountability, and measurable ROI.

Those owners are far more likely to buy a **done-with-you or done-for-you growth partnership** than a standalone course. In fact, positioning your course as a support tool inside a higher-touch program, rather than as the primary product, is likely to attract a much higher-value client.
